subject: CI/CD change-tempo reconciliation & secrets inventory request
messages:
From: Morgan Ellison <morgan.ellison@trust-assessors.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: CI/CD change-tempo reconciliation + secrets inventory

Hi Jonas,

We're scoping the SIG intake for AtlasBank and need a compact package showing how Redwood reconciles change tempo (frequency of deploys/patches) with CI/CD approvals and secrets handling. Specifically please provide: 
- A short CSV or spreadsheet summarizing deploy/change events per environment (prod/stage) for the last 90 days, indicating PR gating decisions and emergency exceptions.
- Evidence of secret handling for CI runners: rotation cadence for any ephemeral tokens, how keystore rotation is logged, and examples (redacted) of rotation audit rows.
- A machine-readable PR-gating matrix (simple table) showing required checks by branch and environment.

Can you confirm whether you can produce these artifacts by COB Pacific on Wednesday (2026-11-11)? If you need a narrower scope we can accept a 30-day window first.

Thanks,
Morgan
Morgan Ellison
Senior Assessor, Trust Assessors

--
Attachment request: sample CSVs and any redaction guidance appreciated.

Morgan —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can deliver a focused packet covering the 90-day window; I think that will be most useful for SIG reviewers. Plan:

1) Attachments (initial):
   - cicd_change_tempo_summary.csv (CSV, ~8KB): deploy/change counts by day, environment, PR-id, gate status.
   - pr-gating-matrix.pdf (PDF, ~160KB): matrix mapping branch -> required checks -> deploy permission.
   - keystore_rotation_snapshot.csv (CSV, ~6KB): redacted rotation audit rows (timestamp, key-id obfuscated, rotation-type).

2) Short narrative (inline below) explaining how we handle emergency patches and temporary bypasses, and where those exceptions are recorded.

3) Delivery: We will upload the files to a shared Drive link and email you a redacted sample here by EOD Wed (2026-11-11). If you prefer a 30-day extract we can do that earlier (tomorrow).

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEXAMPLE (will populate by Wed)
JIRA tracking: SEC-4821 (internal)

If AtlasBank needs machine-readable logs beyond the CSVs (JSONL audit stream), let us know and we can include a one-off export, redacted.

Jonas

Thanks Jonas — quick clarifications from AtlasBank: 

- For the keystore rotation snapshot, can you include the rotation frequency policy (e.g., automated monthly, exception flows) and whether rotation events trigger KMS/ audit entries we can map back to identities? A redacted sample row is fine.
- For emergency bypasses: we need to see the approval trail (who authorized, how was the approval captured) and whether the bypasses are time-limited. If you have a short example of an emergency patch workflow (3–5 lines) that shows the cadence from PR to deploy and backfill remediation, that will suffice.

One other ask: can REDACTED fields be clearly labeled in the CSV so our tooling can accept the exports without additional transformation?

Morgan

Morgan / Alex —

Attaching the requested artifacts (redacted stubs included). Short notes below each file name in the Drive folder. We labeled any redacted fields with the literal string "REDACTED" so your ingestion tooling will see it.

Attachments uploaded to Drive (visible at link):
- cicd_change_tempo_summary.csv — contains date, env, pr_id, gate_status, approver_id (approver_id values are hashed; see README row).
- pr-gating-matrix.pdf — definitive mapping of branch protections and automated checks (unit, lint, security-scan) required before deploy to stage/prod.
- keystore_rotation_snapshot.csv — rows show timestamp, key_alias (REDACTED), rotation_type, rotation_initiator (system/service-account or user-hash).

Emergency patch workflow (short):
1) Triage ticket opened in Incident queue.
2) Patch PR created and flagged EMERGENCY in title.
3) Single-authorizer approval logged in PR as a comment from a repo-admin role; approval captured by the PR webhook and referenced in the generated deploy ticket.
4) Deploy executed via a gated runner that requires the labeled EMERGENCY token; deployment is time-limited and automatically rolled back if a subsequent verification step fails within 30 minutes.
5) Post-deploy remediation: normal PR review and follow-up fixes are required within one business day; exceptions are tracked under JIRA SEC-4821.

If you need additional CSV columns (e.g., raw webhook IDs or full user emails) we can provide those under a redaction NDA; the current exports are intended for SIG intake.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Manager, Platform Security
Redwood Inference
